title: Huawei Plans Non-Folding Widescreen Flagship With Unusual 16:10 Display
excerpt: Leaked specs reveal a candybar-style phone with a 6.39-inch wide display, Kirin 9000 series chip, and a 7,000mAh battery, targeted for a December 2026 launch.
body:
• Huawei is developing a non-folding smartphone with a 16:10 aspect ratio display — significantly wider than the standard 20:9 format used by most flagships.
  • Leaked specifications include a 6.39-inch 2K-class display, Kirin 9000 series chipset, 7,000mAh battery with wireless charging, and a dual 50MP camera system with periscope telephoto.
  • The device draws design inspiration from Huawei's Pura X foldable but in a traditional candybar form factor, targeted at the mid-to-high-end market.
  • A December 2026 launch has been tentatively flagged, positioned after the Mate 90 series.

Huawei is developing a non-folding flagship smartphone with a wider-than-usual display, according to multiple leaks from Chinese tech tipsters. The device would bring the wider screen proportions of Huawei's Pura X foldable to a traditional slab-style phone — without the hinge, the price premium, or the durability trade-offs, GSMArena reported.

Tipsters Digital Chat Station and Smart Pikachu shared details of the device on Weibo, describing an engineering prototype with a 6.39-inch display in a 16:10 aspect ratio. That is visibly wider than the standard 20:9 slab that has dominated flagship smartphone design for years, according to Gizchina.

Specs and Camera System

According to GSMArena, the leaked specifications point to a 2K-class resolution display, a Kirin 9-series chipset, and a battery with a capacity of 7,000mAh or more. Wireless charging is also expected.

The camera system pairs a 50MP primary sensor on a 1/1.3-inch format with a 50MP periscope telephoto and a multispectral sensor for enhanced color accuracy and light processing. The dual 50MP setup at different focal lengths offers genuine versatility beyond the typical wide-plus-ultrawide-plus-telephoto spread, Gizchina noted.

Digital Chat Station, who reportedly saw the engineering prototype, described the device as "surprisingly compact given the wider footprint," noting it felt thin and light in hand, per Gizchina.

Why 16:10 Matters

The aspect ratio shift sounds minor but has meaningful practical implications. At 6.39 inches in a 16:10 format, the device would be closer to the inner display of a compact foldable than a standard slab, Gizchina reported. The extra horizontal space directly improves split-screen multitasking, widescreen video playback, and document reading.

"Huawei already proved the format has appeal with the Pura X foldable. This would be the same concept without the hinge, the price premium, or the durability compromise."

— Gizchina analysis

Huawei's Pura X foldable launched with a 16:10 aspect ratio when unfolded and was considered a commercial success in China. The company also recently launched the Pura X Max, a wider-format foldable that beat Samsung and Apple to market with a book-style design, according to Android Authority.

Market Positioning

Smart Pikachu described the device as targeting the "mid-to-high-end market" — deliberately below the Mate series flagship ceiling, Gizchina reported. A 7,000mAh battery, Kirin 9000 series silicon, and a genuinely differentiated screen format at a sub-Mate price point could carve out a distinct niche.

GSMArena reported that the smartphone could launch between October and December 2026, with Huawei expecting strong sales in China based on the Pura X's market performance. The device is positioned to arrive after the Mate 90 series, according to Gizchina.

What's Next

Details on international availability and final pricing remain unclear at the prototype stage. For now, the device represents Huawei's continued push to differentiate in a market where most flagship phones look virtually identical from the front. Whether the wider form factor translates from concept to commercial hit will depend on the final design, pricing, and how consumers adapt to a phone that feels more like a mini-tablet in hand.
nri_angle: Huawei's widescreen format could interest tech-savvy diaspora consumers looking for differentiated alternatives to the identical-looking Samsung and Apple flagships.
author: Diaspora Desk
